title: Two pronouns together: je te le donne, il y en a
summary: Put two object pronouns in the right order before the verb, in the passé composé, before an infinitive, in the negative and in the imperative.
focus: The fixed order of two object pronouns, and how the imperative changes it
content:
## The order of two pronouns

When a verb has two object pronouns, they always come in this order, before the verb:

| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| me, te, se, nous, vous | le, la, les | lui, leur | y | en |

- **Je te le donne.** — I give it to you.
- **Je le lui donne.** — I give it to him / her.
- **Il y en a.** — There is some / there are some.
- **Je leur en parle.** — I talk to them about it.

Before **y** and **en**, **me, te, se** become **m', t', s'**: **Il m'en reste deux.** — I have two left. **Je t'en prie.**

## Passé composé and infinitives

In the **passé composé**, both pronouns go before **avoir** (or être). A direct object **le / la / les** placed before avoir makes the participle agree:

- **La lettre ? Je la lui ai donnée.** — The letter? I gave it to him.
- **Les photos ? Elle nous les a montrées.** — The photos? She showed them to us.
- **Des pommes ? J'en ai acheté.** — Apples? I bought some. (no agreement with **en**)

With a verb + **infinitive**, they go before the infinitive:

- **Je vais te l'envoyer.** — I'm going to send it to you.
- **Tu peux me les prêter ?** — Can you lend them to me?

## In the negative

**Ne** comes before the two pronouns; **pas** comes after the conjugated verb, or after avoir in the passé composé. The pronoun pair is never split:

- **Je ne te le donne pas.** — I'm not giving it to you.
- **Je ne le lui ai pas dit.** — I didn't tell him / her.
- **Il n'y en a plus.** — There isn't any left.
- **Je ne vais pas te l'envoyer.** — I'm not going to send it to you. (here **ne… pas** wraps aller, the conjugated verb)

## The imperative

In the **affirmative imperative**, the pronouns go **after** the verb, joined by hyphens, direct before indirect, and **me / te** become **moi / toi**:

- **Donne-le-moi !** — Give it to me!
- **Montrez-les-leur.** — Show them to them.
- **Donnez-m'en.** — Give me some. (moi + en → **m'en**)
- **Vas-y !** — Go on! (the -s comes back before y and en: **manges-en**)

In the **negative imperative**, everything goes back to the normal order before the verb:

- **Ne me le dis pas !** — Don't tell me!
- **Ne lui en donne pas.** — Don't give him any.

vocabulary.example: Ton dictionnaire ? Je te le prête jusqu'à lundi.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Your dictionary? I'll lend it to you until Monday.

vocabulary.example: Mes livres ? Il me les a rendus hier.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My books? He gave them back to me yesterday.

vocabulary.example: Le document ? Je vais vous l'envoyer par mail.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The document? I'll send it to you by e-mail.
Your holiday photos? Show them to me!

vocabulary.example: Cette règle ? Le professeur nous l'a expliquée deux fois.
vocabulary.example_meaning: That rule? The teacher explained it to us twice.

vocabulary.example: Cette histoire ? Ma grand-mère me la racontait souvent.
vocabulary.example_meaning: That story? My grandmother often told it to me.

vocabulary.example: Du vin ? Nos amis nous en apportent toujours.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Wine? Our friends always bring us some.

vocabulary.meaning: there is some, there are some
vocabulary.example: Des chaises ? Il y en a dans la cuisine.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Chairs? There are some in the kitchen.

vocabulary.example: La clé de la voiture ? Je ne te la donne pas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The car key? I'm not giving it to you.

vocabulary.example: Le colis ? Le facteur le lui a laissé devant la porte.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The parcel? The postman left it for him in front of the door.

quiz.prompt: Tu me prêtes ton vélo ? — Oui, je ___ prête.
quiz.explanation: Me / te / se / nous / vous come before le / la / les: je te le prête. Le lui would mean 'to him / her', not 'to you'.

quiz.prompt: Tu me rends mes clés ? — Oui, je ___ rends tout de suite.
quiz.explanation: To you = te, the keys = les; te comes first: je te les rends.
hints: Me / te come before le / la / les.

quiz.prompt: Il reste du pain ? — Oui, ___ a encore un peu.
quiz.explanation: Y always comes before en: il y en a. Le cannot replace du pain, which is a partitive: that is en's job.

quiz.prompt: Tu as parlé du voyage à tes parents ? — Oui, je ___ ai parlé.
quiz.explanation: À tes parents = leur, du voyage = en. Leur comes before en, and both go before avoir: je leur en ai parlé.
hints: Parler à quelqu'un de quelque chose.
Lui / leur come before y and en.

quiz.prompt: In 'La lettre ? Je la lui ai donnée', donnée agrees because la stands for la lettre and comes before avoir.
quiz.explanation: A direct object pronoun (le, la, les) placed before avoir makes the participle agree: la → donnée. Lui is indirect and changes nothing.
hints: Which pronoun is the direct object?

quiz.prompt: Tu vas envoyer la photo à ta grand-mère ? — Oui, ___.
quiz.explanation: The pronouns belong to envoyer, so they go before the infinitive, la before lui: je vais la lui envoyer.
hints: Which verb do the pronouns belong to?
Le / la / les come before lui / leur.

quiz.prompt: Tu as montré les photos à Marc ? — Non, je ne ___ ai pas montrées.
quiz.explanation: The photos = les, to Marc = lui; les before lui, both between ne and avoir: je ne les lui ai pas montrées (agreement with les).
hints: Ne goes before the two pronouns, pas after avoir.

quiz.prompt: Le sel est près de toi ? ___, s'il te plaît !
quiz.explanation: In the affirmative imperative, the pronouns follow the verb with hyphens, direct (le) before indirect (moi): passe-le-moi.

quiz.prompt: 'Donnez-moi-en' is the standard way to say 'give me some'.
quiz.explanation: Before en, moi becomes m': donnez-m'en.
hints: What happens to moi before a vowel?

conversations.title: Moving day
conversations.scenario: Camille is moving into a new flat; her friend Yanis has borrowed some of her things to help.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Yanis, tu as toujours ma perceuse ?
lines.meaning: Yanis, do you still have my drill?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, je te la rends demain, promis.
lines.meaning: Yes, I'll give it back to you tomorrow, I promise.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Super. Et les cartons, tu les as donnés à Sophie ?
lines.meaning: Great. And the boxes, did you give them to Sophie?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oui, je les lui ai donnés hier soir.
lines.meaning: Yes, I gave them to her last night.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Non, il n'y en a plus. Je t'en achète ?
lines.meaning: No, there's none left. Shall I buy you some?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Oui, achètes-en deux rouleaux, s'il te plaît.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: D'accord. Et la clé du nouvel appartement ?
lines.meaning: OK. And the key to the new flat?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Le propriétaire va me l'envoyer lundi.
lines.meaning: The landlord is going to send it to me on Monday.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ne la perds pas, et montre-moi l'appartement vite !
lines.meaning: Don't lose it, and show me the flat soon!

listening.text: Il y en a trois dans le tiroir.
listening.meaning: There are three of them in the drawer.
listening.note: New word: le tiroir = the drawer.

listening.text: Elle me l'a envoyé ce matin.
listening.meaning: She sent it to me this morning.

listening.text: Ne me le dis pas maintenant.
listening.note: Negative imperative: the pronouns go before the verb.

listening.text: Je vais vous les montrer tout de suite.
listening.meaning: I'm going to show them to you right away.

listening.text: Mon voisin m'a prêté sa tondeuse et je la lui rends ce soir.
listening.meaning: My neighbour lent me his lawnmower and I'm giving it back to him tonight.
listening.note: New word: la tondeuse = the lawnmower.

listening.text: Des cerises ? Prends-en autant que tu veux.
listening.meaning: Cherries? Take as many as you like.
listening.note: New word: la cerise = the cherry.

listening.text: Nous ne leur en avons jamais parlé.
listening.meaning: We've never talked to them about it.

guide.tip: Say the chain out loud until it sticks: me-te-se-nous-vous, le-la-les, lui-leur, y, en.

concept.title: Me + lui? Never
concept.markdown: Two pronouns from the same column never stand together. With **me, te, nous, vous** as the direct object, the indirect person stays after **à**: **Il me présente à elle.** — He introduces me to her. Never *il me lui présente*.

bites.title: The chain
bites.rule: Two pronouns before the verb always line up: me/te/se/nous/vous → le/la/les → lui/leur → y → en.

bites.title: Before avoir, before the infinitive
bites.rule: Passé composé: both before avoir, and the participle agrees with le/la/les. Verb + infinitive: both before the infinitive.

bites.title: Ne… pas around the pair
bites.rule: Ne comes before the two pronouns, pas after the conjugated verb or avoir. Never split the pair.
bites.example: Je ne le lui ai pas dit.

bites.title: The imperative flips it
bites.rule: Affirmative imperative: after the verb, hyphens, direct first, moi/toi (m' before en). Negative imperative: the normal order.

sorts.title: Right order or wrong?
sorts.why: Me/te before le/la/les, le/la/les before lui/leur, and y before en: the chain never changes before a verb.

sorts.title: Before or after the verb?
sorts.why: Only the affirmative imperative puts the pronouns after the verb; everywhere else, including the negative imperative, they go before.

spots.sentence: La lettre ? Je la lui ai donné hier.
spots.why: La (the letter) comes before avoir, so the participle agrees: donnée.

spots.sentence: Tu as du gâteau ? Donne-moi-en un peu.
spots.why: Before en, moi becomes m': donne-m'en.
Before y, the tu imperative of aller takes back its -s: vas-y.

spots.sentence: Les photos ? Je les leur ai montré.
spots.why: Les (the photos, feminine plural) comes before avoir: montrées.
In the negative imperative, the pronouns go back before the verb: ne me le dis pas.
